newsitem.title: FRANCE: TF1 falls on weak 1996 results.
newsitem.headline: TF1 falls on weak 1996 results.

text.p: Shares in French television company TF1 fell on Wednesday as analysts pointed to its loss of audience share and the launch cost of the TPS digital television service revealed in 1996 profits, down 8.6 percent.
TF1 traded down four percent at 486.7 francs on volume of 86,997 shares at 1146 GMT.
"Just as TF1 is confronted with investment for TPS (Television par Satellite), it is faced with an erosion in the channel and shrinking advertising revenues," an analyst said.
TF1 saw a 1.9 percent decline in audience share in 1996.
"Advertising revenues rose 4.4 percent in the first half of 1996 and the year ended with an increase of 1.1 percent, so the second half was pretty bad," the analyst said.
The company, in a departure from previous practice, is discounting advertising rates as the volume of advertising has risen six percent, another market professional said.

TF1 also faces competition from other channels, such as M6, which wants to attract key audiences, said the professional, who expects the trend in falling profit to be long term and forecasts a double-digit drop in 1997 profit.
TF1, 39 percent owned by construction company Bouygues, reported 1996 net attributable profit of 550 million francs, down from 602 million.
It cited the launch cost of TPS and 35 million francs in writedown of goodwill on acquisitions.
TPS is due to receive an after-tax payment of 140 million francs from TF1 this year, TPS and TF1 chairman Patrick Le Lay said at the beginning of January.
